To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

microglial cells produce extracellular vesicles that contain endocannabinoids, and that these extracellular vesicles are able to stimulate CB1 receptors and inhibit GABAergic transmission in target neurons.
endocannabinoid AEA is transported through extracellular membrane‐bound vesicles and that these vesicles are produced by microglia and are able to cross the blood–brain barrier.

microglial cells secrete endocannabinoids through extracellular vesicles, and that the endocannabinoids carried on the vesicles are able to activate CB1 receptors on GABAergic neurons and inhibit presynaptically GABA release.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of extracellular vesicles as a novel mode of transport of endocanabinoids in the brain.
the role of microglia in the extracellular transport and function of endocannabinoid signaling in the central nervous system.
the identification of the mechanisms of endocannabinoid transport in the nervous system, and the demonstration of a new mode of endocannabinod signalling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

microglia can release endocannabinoids through extracellular vesicles, which are able to activate the CB1 receptor and to inhibit GABA release from GABAergic neurons, thus providing a novel mechanism for the modulation of neuronal activity by endocannabinoids.
extracellular vesicles are a novel mechanism for intercellular communication between microglia and neurons, and that endocannabinoid vesicles are involved in the modulation of synaptic activity.
extracellular vesicles are involved in the transport of endocanbinoids, and this transport is functional.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
microglial cells secrete endocannabinoids on extracellular vesicles to regulate neuronal synaptic communication.
endocannabinoid‐containing extracellular vesicles released by microglia act as a novel intercellular signaling system that regulates synaptic transmission.

microglial cells secrete AEA‐containing vesicles to target neurons, which in turn can activate CB1 receptors on the surface of target neurons, and inhibit presynaptically GABAergic synaptic transmission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
extracellular vesicles are an important mechanism for intercellular communication in the brain.
extracellular vesicles are a novel mechanism for the transport of endogenous lipophilic signaling molecules, such as endocannabinoids, across cell membranes.

endocannabinoid signalling is not only restricted to the nervous system but also occurs in a paracrine way, through extracellular vesicles, and that endocannabinoidal signalling can be modulated by microglia.
